items.stem:
Which of the following statement(s) is (are) true about heart?
(i) Left atrium receives oxygenated blood from different parts of body while right atrium receives deoxygenated blood from lungs.
(ii) Left ventricle pumps oxygenated blood to different body parts while right ventricle pumps deoxygenated blood to lungs.
(iii) Left atrium transfers oxygenated blood to right ventricle which sends it to different body parts.
(iv) Right atrium receives deoxygenated blood from different parts of the body while left ventricle pumps oxygenated blood to different parts of the body.
items.answer: (c) (ii) and (iv). Only statements (ii) and (iv) are correct. Statement (i) is wrong because the left atrium receives oxygenated blood from the lungs and the right atrium receives deoxygenated blood from the body; statement (iii) is wrong because the left atrium passes blood to the left ventricle, not the right ventricle.

items.stem: What prevents back flow of blood inside the heart during contraction?
items.answer: (a) Valves in heart. Valves guard the openings between the atria and the ventricles and at the base of the great arteries, so they permit blood to flow in one direction only and prevent its back flow when the heart contracts.

items.stem: Single circulation, i.e., blood flows through the heart only once during one cycle of passage through the body, is exhibited by
items.answer: (b) Hippocampus, Exocoetus, Anabas. All three are fishes, and fishes have a two-chambered heart through which blood passes only once in a complete cycle, i.e. single circulation.

items.stem: In which of the following vertebrate group/groups, heart does not pump oxygenated blood to different parts of the body?
items.answer: (d) Pisces only. In fishes the two-chambered heart pumps only deoxygenated blood to the gills, where it is oxygenated and then supplied directly to the body, so the heart itself never pumps oxygenated blood.
items.ocr: Printed as 'vertebrate group groups'; read as 'vertebrate group/groups'.

items.stem: Choose the correct statement that describes arteries.

options.label: A
options.text: They have thick elastic walls, blood flows under high pressure; collect blood from different organs and bring to the heart.

options.label: B
options.text: They have thin walls with valves inside, blood flows under low pressure and carry blood away from the heart to various organs of the body.

options.label: C
options.text: They have thick elastic walls, blood flows under low pressure; carry blood from the heart to various organs of the body.

options.label: D
options.text: They have thick elastic walls without valves inside, blood flows under high pressure and carry blood away from the heart to different parts of the body.

items.answer: (d) They have thick elastic walls without valves inside, blood flows under high pressure and carry blood away from the heart to different parts of the body.

items.stem: The filtration units of kidneys are called
items.answer: (d) nephrons. Each kidney contains a very large number of nephrons (uriniferous tubules), which are the basic structural and functional filtration units of the kidney.
items.ocr: Option label (a) was damaged to a bare 'a ureter'; restored as option A.

items.stem: Oxygen liberated during photosynthesis comes from
items.answer: (a) water. During the light reaction of photosynthesis, water molecules are split (photolysis) into hydrogen and oxygen, and it is this oxygen that is released into the atmosphere.

items.stem: The blood leaving the tissues becomes richer in
items.answer: (a) carbon dioxide. At the tissues, oxygen diffuses from the blood into the cells while the carbon dioxide produced by respiration diffuses from the cells into the blood, so the blood leaving the tissues is rich in carbon dioxide.

items.stem: Which of the following is an incorrect statement?

options.label: B
options.text: Organisms must repair and maintain their structure.

options.label: C
options.text: Movement of molecules does not take place among cells.

options.label: D
options.text: Energy is essential for life processes.

items.answer: (c) Movement of molecules does not take place among cells. This statement is incorrect because molecules are continuously exchanged between cells and their surroundings by diffusion and other transport processes; the other three statements are true of all living organisms.
items.ocr: Two repairs: (1) option label (c) was lost - the text 'Movement of molecules does not take place among cells.' printed without a label and ran on from option (b), restored as option C from the printed key 'Ans (c)'; (2) option (d) printed as 'Energy is essential for live processes.', corrected to 'life processes'.

items.stem: The internal (cellular) energy reserve in autotrophs is
items.answer: (c) Starch. Autotrophs (green plants) convert the extra glucose made during photosynthesis into starch, which is stored inside the cells and acts as their internal energy reserve.
